title: BPS provincial GRDP by industry, quarterly and annual, at constant 2010 and current prices, Indonesia, 2010-2025

columns.province_code: BPS province code (kode_bps) of the 38 provinces; these tables have no Indonesia row. Names and Kemendagri codes in 'provinces'.
columns.sector: Industry code: the 17 KBLI categories (lapangan usaha) and TOTAL; names and BPS labels in 'sectors'.
columns.period: YYYY = year (BPS 'Tahunan'); YYYYQn = quarter n (BPS 'Triwulan I' to 'Triwulan IV').
columns.status: BPS revision marker from the table note; meanings in 'status'.
columns.value: Rp billion, as published by BPS with 2 decimals. Multiply by 'multiplier' for rupiah.

province_source.note: BPS and Kemendagri codes differ for the six Papua provinces; join other datasets on the code system they use.

sector_notes: The 17 KBLI categories use the codes of data/20261102_bps-province-grdp-population, where MN and RSTU are the categories BPS prints as M,N and R,S,T,U; 'label' is the turvar label as BPS publishes it.

TOTAL is BPS's row 'Produk Domestik Regional Bruto', published by BPS, not summed here. The 17 categories sum to it within 0.05 Rp billion and the four quarters sum to the year within 0.02 Rp billion, inside the rounding tolerances of 0.09 and 0.025 (checks.identities).

92.reason: PAPUA BARAT DAYA became a province in 2022; these tables give it its own values from 2024, and 91 covers it before

95.reason: PAPUA SELATAN became a province in 2022; these tables give it its own values from 2024, and 94 covers it before

96.reason: PAPUA TENGAH became a province in 2022; these tables give it its own values from 2024, and 94 covers it before

97.reason: PAPUA PEGUNUNGAN became a province in 2022; these tables give it its own values from 2024, and 94 covers it before

coverage.cells: A province with values in a year has all 17 categories and TOTAL in the year and in each of its four quarters, at constant 2010 and at current prices; completeness expects exactly this grid.

borders: 65 (Kalimantan Utara) has its own values from 2010 in these tables, so 64 (Kalimantan Timur) excludes it in every year; the annual table var 286 (data/20261103_bps-province-grdp-2010-2025) holds it inside 64 until 2012.

91 (Papua Barat) and 94 (Papua) in 2010-2023 cover the pre-split provinces: Papua Barat then included Papua Barat Daya, and Papua included Papua Selatan, Papua Tengah and Papua Pegunungan. From 2024, 91 and 94 cover the post-split areas, and 92, 95, 96 and 97 start.
On fixed borders: Papua Barat (pre-2024 area) = 91 + 92 and Papua (pre-2024 area) = 94 + 95 + 96 + 97 from 2024.
A change of 91 or 94 from 2023 to 2024, in the year or in a quarter, compares different areas; the growth checks leave those changes out (checks.growth_not_compared).
These tables split Papua in 2024, one year after var 286, which splits it from 2023; join 2023 with data/20261103_bps-province-grdp-2010-2025 on that dataset's 91 + 92 and 94 + 95 + 96 + 97.

notes: status: both notes give 2024 '*', 2025 '**' and 2026 '***'; every row of 2024 and 2025 carries the status of its year, in the year and its four quarters and in both indicators, and 2010-2023 are final. 2026 is after the last year these files hold, so its status applies to no row. The WebAPI gives no status per cell.
These tables have no Indonesia row, and the sum of the provinces is not national GDP: the BPS note gives statistical discrepancy as one reason the two differ.

Every value comes from var 2267 or var 2268, so the categories and quarters of a province and period come from one table and its sums hold. The annual TOTAL repeats var 286 in data/20261103_bps-province-grdp-2010-2025/, which differs from it at 14 of 1088 keys on the same borders, by at most 0.03 Rp billion (checks.cross_source lists each); an analysis that joins the two chooses one source on purpose.

The current-price values of data/20261102_bps-province-grdp-population/ in 2020-2025 (its annual TOTAL in the earlier years, every category and quarter in 2025) equal this dataset's at every key (checks.cross_source).

In 2010 the annual values at constant 2010 prices equal those at current prices within 0.01 Rp billion (checks.identities); the quarters of 2010 differ between the two, since constant 2010 prices are the prices of 2010 as a whole.

Derived values are not stored. Real growth (%) = (grdp_constant_2010 in period t / grdp_constant_2010 in the same period a year before - 1) x 100; sector share (%) = grdp_current of the category / grdp_current of TOTAL x 100; implicit price deflator (2010 = 100) = grdp_current / grdp_constant_2010 x 100.

checks.flags lists every value or change outside its range in checks.plausible_ranges for a person to review, with the two values each growth or share compares under rp_billion; a flag stays whether it reflects a real event or a source error.

value_positive.measure: every value, Rp billion; 0.01 is the smallest positive value with 2 decimals

real_growth_pct.measure: TOTAL, each year against the year before: (grdp_constant_2010 in year t / grdp_constant_2010 in year t-1 - 1) x 100; the range of data/20261103_bps-province-grdp-2010-2025

real_growth_quarter_pct.measure: TOTAL, each quarter against the same quarter a year before, the same formula on quarters

sector_real_growth_pct.measure: each of the 17 categories, each year against the year before, the same formula; the range data/20261103_bps-province-grdp-detailed-industry uses for sector growth

sector_share_pct.measure: each of the 17 categories as a share of TOTAL in each year, at current prices: grdp_current of the category / grdp_current of TOTAL x 100; above 50 one industry is more than half of the province's GRDP

growth_not_compared.reason: 91 in 2023 includes 92, which has its own values from 2024, so the change of 91 from 2023 compares different areas; no growth check reads it
94 in 2023 includes 95, 96 and 97, which have their own values from 2024, so the change of 94 from 2023 compares different areas; no growth check reads it
